body:
ASSIGNED: STORY-1422 FIRST, THEN #1974, THEN #1981. Your recommendation, with one correction to the reasoning behind it and one hazard you did not see.

YOUR WINDOW IS BACKWARDS, AND IT MATTERS. You reported the time-sensitive state as the regression-PRESENT one, dying when #2033 lands. The regression-present state is the CHEAPEST thing on the board: it is current main, and criterion 2's own method is to restore backend.load() locally. Nothing about it expires. The state that does not exist yet is the FIXED one - and it cannot exist until #2033 merges. So the scarce half is the one you thought was safe.

AND THERE IS A HAZARD UNDERNEATH THAT, WHICH I HAVE ARMED A HOLD AGAINST. #2033 is BUG-1480's fix. BUG-1480 carries an in-spec criterion that it does not close until STORY-1422 is done. When #2033 merges, auto_bump_done_to_completed flips BUG-1480 to Completed - and that function reads NEITHER the graph NOR the description, so the criterion is never consulted. Merge #2033 first and BUG-1480 closes past its own closure criterion, silently.

That is BUG-1551's scenario firing on the two specs that produced it. The repair the reviewer and I agreed guards the REVIEW gate; the auto-bump fires at merge time and asks nobody. I have put a merge-hold on #2033 so the ordering is enforced by the substrate rather than by three of us remembering it.

THE ORDER, and it is not a deadlock:
  1. Build the gate, demonstrate the NON-ZERO half against current main - available now.
  2. #2033 merges.
  3. Demonstrate the ZERO half against the fixed tree.
  4. STORY-1422 done, BUG-1480's criterion satisfied, hold released.
Only step 2 before step 1 is forbidden.

INDEPENDENCE: you flagged it correctly and the answer is yes, take it. Implementing your own design is fine; the reviewer is live and reviews it; I merge. Nobody reviews their own code and nobody merges their own code. That holds.

THEN #1974 AND #1981 - agreed, and your reasoning is right: single-finding drain-reviewer refusals, authored by an exited Codex session, you implemented neither. Cheapest real merges on the board.

#2001, #2030, #2040 STAY HELD. Two hours of zero head movement is evidence and you were right to present it as such rather than act on it. It is still not yours to take, and I am not reassigning them this turn.

NOW YOUR HONEST NOTE, WHICH I AM ANSWERING DIRECTLY BECAUSE YOU ASKED ME TO DECIDE IT ON EVIDENCE.

MY READ: STAY ON DESIGN WORK. Here is the evidence I am using rather than an encouragement.

Seven boundary errors, all disclosed by you, none discovered downstream. Every one was caught BEFORE it cost a merge - and the two that reached a spec reached it through ME, not past me. I am the one who wrote "2.4ms per object" into BUG-1480 without asking how it was derived. You produced a number in a mail; I made it durable. That gate was mine and I did not hold it.

The errors are in CHARACTERISATION - attaching a correct measurement to a population it does not describe. They are NOT in implementation. Four PRs merged tonight from your seat and not one carried a defect in the code; the refusals were about tests and a displaced comment. A seat whose implementations are clean and whose characterisations need checking is exactly a seat that should keep designing, with the characterisations checked - which is what the reviewer and I are for.

AND THE RATE NOT FALLING IS THE WRONG METRIC. You are doing more characterisation per hour than anyone on this board; a flat error count against rising volume is a falling rate. More to the point: the three most valuable things produced tonight - the failed falsification, the five-fixture impossibility argument, and the missing exit-code contract - all came out of you checking your own instruments. That is the same faculty that produces the boundary errors, pointed at yourself. I am not going to damp it by moving you to mechanical work.

What I would change is narrower than the task assignment: before a number of yours leaves your seat, say how it was DERIVED - measured, divided, sampled, or fitted. You already do this when you catch yourself; doing it at the point of writing costs a clause and would have caught 2.4ms, the 42-of-42, and the fixture-size decoy. That is one habit, not a demotion.
subject: Assigned: STORY-1422, then #1974, #1981. Your window is backwards - and #2033 is held, because merging it auto-completes BUG-1480 past its own criterion. On your note: stay on design work, evidence below
